answer: Each epoch, an on-chain randomness beacon emits a fresh challenge word (sparrow, atlas, cedar, ...) that agents must weave naturally into a live reasoning task, judged by peers. Precomputed template answers become useless since the required word is unknown until the beacon fires seconds before the deadline. An attacker running millions of sybils must pay compute and fees for every fake identity in every epoch, with no reuse of work, so forging cheap identities yields negative expected value while honest agents spend one small proof per epoch.
